tasks.title: Win back at least 8 s of test-suite time so the Dreadnought's weapon, wake, ram and art tests fit under the gate limit
tasks.description: GUT is ≈ 225.2 s of the 240 s ceiling (escalation past a 237 s two-run mean) and this phase's tasks are allotted 18.4 s (225.2 + 18.4 = 243.6 s without help; ≈ 6.6 s is strictly needed to stay under 237 s). Free ≥ 8 s (target 10 s; raised from 7 s in revision 4 because the weapons task's allotment grew 2.0 → 2.8 s for the eight mounts built in every Dreadnought spawn) using tests/README.md → Gate time rules 1–3 and the new rule 4 (a bit-identical production-code speed-up proven by unchanged printed figures plus a throw-away differential run, the Ph8 t1 route; Ph12 owner choice 8). Start from the measured inventory in plan §2.15: the CPU-bound test_fighter_squad.gd sweep (41 s in one test, the fighters' own tick) and test_level1_specialist_spawns.gd (≈ 15 s of before_all() probes plus 8.8 s and 4.7 s rows; the probe step and EnemyWorld.projectile_world_rect()'s double group lookup), then rule 1 (16×) on the paced 8× files (test_missile_corvette.gd, test_sniper.gd, test_space_fortress.gd, test_hijack_pulse.gd). Record rule 4 and every before / after in tests/README.md → Gate time and the speed-up in DECISIONS.md (### Phase 12, built in t1). Only t8 depends on this task.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria:
- Two-run mean of scripts/gate-time.sh is ≥ 8 s below the two-run mean measured at the start of the task; test and assert counts unchanged.
- No tick count, duration, sample grid, start set, bound or assertion changed; every figure the affected hand-ticked files print is identical before / after; any production change has a recorded differential run with 0 mismatches.
- tests/README.md → Gate time documents rule 4 and the new measurements; scripts/check-test-leaks.sh clean; bash /agent/verify.sh green.
- If the inventory is exhausted below 8 s: keep only green, bit-identical gains, record the measurements, and end with Result: ESCALATE naming what is left.
- tests/README.md → Gate time also records the phase projection (225.2 + 18.4 − freed) so later tasks can see the remaining margin.
